doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Hoagy Carmichael track and a family link
summary: He chose a Carmichael tune and explains his family link and his admiration.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’ll tell you later why I picked this out of this particular set. There’s a reason, not because of my playing, I mean because of a social explanation.
I see you have a vocal on this too.

I sang “I Can’t Get Started.” Not good, but darn it, Bunny wasn’t much of a singer. This is Jack Keller, who lives in Florida. Wendell Marshall, you know played with Duke’s band, a great bass player. I loved Hoagie, and I’ll go into part of the reasoning why, a great writer, a great songwriter. I wish I had had the chance to do an album of him. You know I did others.
Yeah. It’s a challenge writing backgrounds for trumpet and baritone.
Oh, sure, yeah there’s not a whole wealth of color.
I think it holds up well.
Thank you. John is a very complex man. Excellent musician. But you know he really made that Berklee.
Wow. Some interesting chords there at the end.

Thank you. The reason for my picking this is not because of the musical content over any of the other things, but, now I hope I can get this straight, my brother-in-law’s widow is married to Hoagy Carmichael’s stepson. Clear as mud, right? But so we share that. But I loved Hoagy Carmichael, he wrote so many great things, and he never got, I think, the commercial recognition. I mean “Stardust” of course, but so many other tunes that nobody, a lot of people don’t know about.
He went all the way back to Bix’s days too.
Yeah. He and Bix were like friends. Those must have been great days. I’m a little young for that.
